claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a priest (presbyter) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was active in the first half of the fifth century.
According to Theophanes Confessor, Hesychius became presbyter at Jerusalem in 412.
Hesychius of Jerusalem died around 450 or in the 450s.
Hesychius was a celebrated preacher and prolific commentator on the Old and New Testament.
Hesychius composed Homily 8, On Antony, which he preached during the celebration of the saint at the church of the Anastasis in Jerusalem on 17 January.
The homily was written in Greek at Jerusalem in the early 5th century.
The work is an encomium (laudatory speech) on Antony the Great, the monk of Egypt.
The homily compares Antony with biblical figures including Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, David, Daniel, John the Baptist, John the Evangelist, and Paul the Apostle.
The homily praises Antony's life in the light of biblical quotations concerning righteousness.
The work survives as Homily 8 in the collection of Hesychius's homilies, with the title 'In sanctum Antonium' (On Saint Antony).
The work is catalogued as CPG 6572 and BHG 141f in standard repertories of Greek patristic and hagiographic literature.
